displayPattern: Amber status LED on a Carrier 59SC5 stays off. No flashes
meaning: Status LED stays off: the service label says to check for 115 VAC at L1 and L2, and for 24 VAC at SEC-1 and SEC-2.
causes: No 115 VAC at L1 and L2, or no 24 VAC at SEC-1 and SEC-2
diySteps: A dark LED is a status, not a numbered flash code. Write down that it is staying off
Technician: check for 115 VAC at L1 and L2 and 24 VAC at SEC-1 and SEC-2, with power restored only for the measurement
proAdvice: Call a licensed HVAC technician. Measuring line voltage at L1 and L2 is not a homeowner meter job. A steady-on LED is a different status: the control has 24 VAC.
safetyNote: If you smell gas, do not touch any electrical switch or use a phone in the building; leave immediately and call your gas supplier from outside. Turn off electrical power at the furnace switch or breaker before opening any panel, and never bypass or jumper a limit, rollout or pressure switch. Gas valve, burner, venting, wiring and control-board work should be done by a licensed HVAC technician.
sourceTitle: Carrier 59SC5A installation, start-up, operating and service instructions (Catalog No. 59SC5A-01SI), Fig. 55 service label. Read 2026-11-07
